heroHeadline: NUG-PDF Arrests Own Resistance Ally in Sagaing Mining Dispute; KIA Guerrillas Contest Junta Highway Despite 300-Vehicle Reinforcement — Day 1,942
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,942 of Myanmar's civil war (May 28, 2026), a rare internal resistance conflict emerged in Sagaing Region when NUG-affiliated Pa-Ka-Phah forces in Minkin Township detained Ko San Tin Htun, chairman of the Student Revolutionary Force, along with six other SRF members — an incident rooted in disputes over Chindwin River gold mining taxation rights and recruitment authority that exposes structural governance tensions within the anti-junta coalition. Residents protested the arrests. Simultaneously, KIA and allied PDF forces continue contesting the Mandalay–Myitkyina highway corridor through guerrilla ambushes despite the SAC's May 5 recapture of Mawlu and the deployment of a 300-vehicle armored convoy to Myitkyina's Northern Military Command — the largest junta reinforcement to Kachin State in years. The junta's multi-front May 2026 offensive remains acute across five simultaneous theatres: AA forces advancing on China's $7.3B Kyaukphyu CMEC port (50,000+ displaced from Sanae/Kyaukphyu); SAC human shield operations displacing 20,000+ from Butalin, Sagaing (May 27); junta airstrikes killing 3 women in Kyain Seikkyi, Karen State (May 27); Karenni resistance in a new defensive phase after junta counteroffensive around Hpasawng; and 40+ airstrikes on Chin State's Mindat-Kanpetlet corridor in two weeks. UN documents 16.2 million Burmese requiring humanitarian aid — nearly one-third of the population.
